title: The formal layer: every clause in the inventory gets a Lean home (ADR-0025, M2 through M8)
description:
## Problem Statement

The specification set has 497 requirements, six specification gates and a habit of cross-model review, and on 2026-09-12 three defects still landed that every gate and two readers passed: each citation resolved while the consequences contradicted. `LDG-38` described its billing-period reset as the customer's favour when the arithmetic says the opposite; `STO-12` and `STO-13` together demanded something PostgreSQL refuses; `STO-54` and `ADR-0023` called a one-interval grace a repair. The gates check that a rule is cited, owned and phrased; nothing checks what a rule implies, and the one gate that executed anything sampled floating-point inputs and never crossed a period boundary.

The owner's decision (`ADR-0025`) is that the set's precise semantics — calculations, predicates, closed tables and the lifecycle transitions with their real transaction and provider-call boundaries — are carried in Lean under `tools/formal/`, proved for every input, with the historical defects retained as executable witnesses so that "a plausible but incorrect amendment can no longer pass review merely because its prose sounds consistent". The first milestone (arithmetic and witnesses) has landed, been reviewed and been fixed. This spec is the remaining inventory.

## Solution

Extend the formal layer milestone by milestone until every clause in the agreed inventory has a Lean home: the claim model, the cancellation fence composed on it, the closed tables with the rendering gate that keeps the Markdown honest, reconciliation knowledge and restore, funding and the tenant lifecycle, rescue and install, wire canonicalization and redaction. Each milestone lands as theorems over every input, decided witnesses for the historical defects, and a negative theorem for every guard a dated amendment added — refused with the guard, admitted without it — all behind the one specification gate the set already runs, with a CI negative control per check.

Authority follows `ADR-0025`: a formalized clause's home is its tagged declaration; the requirement keeps its identifier, MUST, rationale and retained traps; the rendered formula or table is generated or diffed, never trusted. A theorem is never a conformance item.

## User Stories

1. As a spec author, I want a rule I amend to break a theorem when the amendment contradicts a property the set claims, so that the contradiction is found before review rather than by it.
2. As a spec author, I want the historical defects (`usable_sats > 0`, per-tick rounding, the unfenced funding read, the missing claim term, the period-reset direction) kept as executable witnesses, so that none can be re-laid without a red build.
3. As a spec author, I want every guard a dated amendment added to be a parameter of the model that carries it, so that removing the guard is a one-token change a witness theorem exercises.
4. As a spec author, I want a formalized formula or table rendered into the requirement from its declaration, so that I never maintain two copies by hand.
5. As a spec author, I want a rendered region that carries prose or citations diffed rather than rewritten, so that the rationale and citations around a table survive regeneration.
6. As a spec author, I want a backticked declaration name in a document to be checked against the emitted index, so that a renamed declaration cannot leave a dangling citation.
7. As a spec author, I want the model's identities (`OperationId`, `ClaimNumber`, `EpisodeId`, `MachineId`, `TenantId`) to be distinct types, so that a fence holding an attempt's id instead of an episode's is a type error rather than a review finding.
8. As a spec author, I want "the store committed" and "the worker learned it committed" to be separate facts in the model, so that `ADR-0022`'s lost reply is representable and not collapsed into rollback.
9. As a spec author, I want "dispatched", "applied" and "response received" to be separate facts for a provider call, so that a lost response is never read as evidence nothing happened.
10. As a spec author, I want `OPS-49`'s "never the last failed statement" to be a refuted alternative in the model, so that the prohibited partial-statement retry is expressible and shown harmful.
11. As a spec author, I want both commit orderings of `OPS-42`'s fence proved, so that "one of them provably loses" is a theorem and not a sentence.
12. As a spec author, I want the cancellation model to carry the rate-outage branch, the tenant's current suspension state and the episode, so that the theorem proved is about the requirement as written and not a simplification of it.
13. As a spec author, I want `OPS-33`'s release-without-resolution to be a reachable positive witness (`unknown` knowledge with a closed commitment), so that the model cannot mistake release for absence.
14. As a spec author, I want absence evidence to require a complete pass, an elapsed window and a direct reread as three separate conjuncts, so that dropping any one admits a witness.
15. As a spec author, I want restart and restore to be distinct events with distinct trace types, so that a restart theorem cannot be cited as covering a restore.
16. As a spec author, I want `STO-54`'s "an extension lost in Δ is not rebuilt" to be a proved existential, so that the weaker recovery guarantee is stated by a theorem and not assumed away.
17. As a spec author, I want every closed table (`OPS-11`, `OPS-3`, `OPS-48`, `DOM-31`, the halt matrix) to be a total function whose totality is decided, so that adding a kind without a row fails the build.
18. As a spec author, I want a migration plan's transaction mode to be a type, so that `F52`'s second defect — a `CONCURRENTLY` build inside a transaction — cannot be written.
19. As a spec author, I want the ledger's "consumption leaves `available` unchanged" and the clamp's "the credit is untouched" proved over every input, so that the 2026-09-02 double charge is unrepresentable.
20. As a spec author, I want provider windows, PostgreSQL semantics and `OPS-47`'s single engine to appear as named hypotheses on the theorems that depend on them, so that a signature shows what was assumed.
21. As a reviewer reading a landing without memory of the session, I want the emitted index to say which requirement each declaration formalizes, so that I can check a declaration against the sentence it claims to carry.
22. As a reviewer, I want every proof to rest on the three standard axioms only, with `sorry`, project axioms and `native_decide` refused by the gate, so that a green build means what it says.
23. As a reviewer, I want each new check to have a CI control that breaks the thing it guards and asserts the failure came from that check, so that a red for the wrong reason is never taken as evidence.
24. As CI, I want the formal layer to build and gate in the same job as the textual gates, under the same Nix shell a developer uses, so that there is one toolchain definition.
25. As CI, I want a module the build never imports to be refused, so that a proof file nobody reads is not a green check.
26. As a future implementer, I want the model's definitions to compute permitted outcomes for a sequence of commands and faults, so that an implementation can be compared against them in a test, without that comparison being mistaken for a refinement proof.
27. As a future implementer, I want the conformance checklist to count nothing from the formal layer, so that a proved model never reads as a passed test.
28. As the owner, I want the inventory built in the order that lets each model be true when it lands — claim before fence, tables before the rendering gate, reconciliation and restore before funding — so that no milestone proves a false requirement to save time.
29. As the owner, I want Mathlib added only in a commit naming the theorem that cannot close without it, so that the dependency is never carried by default.
30. As the owner, I want the glossary term **reference model** added when the first lifecycle model exists, so that the glossary never describes an artifact that does not exist.

## Implementation Decisions

**Order and milestones.** Each milestone is one ticket; a milestone's acceptance is a proof or decided check that fails on a named historical defect.

- M2, the claim model (`ADR-0022`, `OPS-5`, `OPS-6`, `OPS-8`, `OPS-22`, `OPS-49`, `STO-3`). A durable row with status and claim number; executions each holding their claim; a transaction as a list of statements with the guarded status write first; whole-transaction restart as the retry, with the last-statement retry definable so it can be refuted; the store outcome as committed-and-acked pairs; the provider outcome as dispatched, applied, reply. Theorems: a stale execution's write is inert after a later claim; a same-claim repetition changes nothing, `revision` included; provider calls across store retries are at most one; a lost reply on the claim itself is a transition to exit and never a re-claim. Witness pair: the stale-defer trace refused with the claim term, admitted without it. Both panel readers proved that pair in scratch; the decision-rich shape, from that prototype:

  ```
  guardOk withClaimTerm row write := row.status = running ∧ (¬withClaimTerm ∨ row.claim = write.mine)
  trace withClaimTerm := A claims (1); A defers; reply lost; B claims (2); A repeats its defer
  refused  : (trace true).status  = running
  admitted : (trace false).status = queued
  ```

- M3, the cancellation fence composed on M2 (`OPS-41`, `OPS-42`, `LDG-62`, `OPS-48`, `LDG-16`, `ADR-0021`). Model state carries the machine's commitment, stored date and `exhausted_since`, the fence as an optional episode id, the episode and its state, the rate as optional (outage is a branch, not a value), the tenant's current suspension state, and time. Events: sweep routing on the stored date and the column, claim, the fence transaction with its re-check inside it as a parameter, extension in its own serialization guarded on the fence, provider delete outside the serialization, reply, settlement, gone-write, retry from stalled only, rate movement. Invariants over reachable states with the single-engine assumption in the signature: destruction only after a fence transaction whose re-check read unfunded, no rate, or suspended; an extension after the fence opens nothing and moves nothing; an extension before the fence is seen by the re-check; a set fence names an open episode with the same id; closed is absorbing; gone clears the fence and closes the episode together. Witnesses, one parameter each: re-check outside the fence transaction, fence holding the attempt id, the withdrawn abort predicate inside the lifecycle, abort without the date write, suspension keyed on episode reasons.

- M4, the closed tables and the rendering gate (`OPS-11`, `OPS-3`, `OPS-48`, `DOM-31`, `DOM-17`). Each table is a total function with a `match` carrying no wildcard, its totality decided. The rendering gate: `lake exe gate` already emits the index; a Python specification gate reads it, diffs every marked region in the documents against what the declaration emits, generates the pure-computation regions, and resolves every backticked declaration name. The citations gate gains that resolver. `check-all.sh` orders the formal build before the gates that read its index. First marked regions: `OPS-48`'s transition table and `DOM-31`'s diagram emitted and diffed; `LDG-38`'s worked examples and `LDG-31`'s worked table generated. The migration-plan type (transactional versus standalone statement) lands here as the formal home of `F52`'s second defect.

- M5, reconciliation knowledge and restore (`OPS-32`, `OPS-33`, `OPS-36`, `OPS-27`, `PRV-36`, `STO-54`, `STO-5`, `OPS-15`). Knowledge as `unknown`, `observed present`, `authoritative absence`, `multiple candidates`, separate from the commitment's open or closed; absence evidence as three conjuncts; two window fields, never one. Fault events `crash`, `restart`, `restore Δ`, `complete procedure` with separate trace types; recovery phases as separate permissions, never one Boolean; quarantine of the irreversible kinds before the first claim; the lost extension not rebuilt as a proved existential.

- M6, funding and the tenant lifecycle (`LDG-8`, `LDG-9`, `LDG-31`, `LDG-70`, `STO-30`, `STO-31`, `WIR-42`, `API-34`, `API-35`). Ledger conservation; the clamp and the deficiency as separate quantities in separate units; rail-identity replay; deposit expiry; tenant deletion; operator attribution.

- M7, rescue and install (`RSC-3`–`RSC-5`, `RSC-26`, `RSC-39`–`RSC-44`, `OPS-45`). Trust state, inventory validation, write-started markers, rescue exit, recovery-key retention. Physical and cryptographic facts are hypotheses.

- M8, wire canonicalization, redaction and admission (`API-9`, `API-12`, `WIR-1a`, `WIR-32`, `API-21`, `STO-50`, `API-7`, `SEC-39`, `LDG-20`, `LDG-40`). Canonical serialization, fingerprint preimage, projection and redaction idempotence, the admission and halt matrices as decided policy spaces. Whether `WIR-37`'s fixtures are generated is decided at the end of M4 on the evidence of the rendering mechanism; if yes, `13-wire-contract.md`'s precedence sentence is amended to say a registered shape renders its declaration.

**Authority and rendering** (`ADR-0025`). One declaration per formalized clause, tagged with the requirement identifier; the requirement keeps identifier, MUST, rationale, amendment record and traps. Until a clause's region is gated, the Markdown is authoritative and the Lean is a checking interpretation. Ids stay append-only; withdrawn definitions live in a historical namespace that current policy cannot select. No hand-kept manifest.

**Trust.** Standard three axioms only, `sorryAx` refused transitively, no project axioms, `native_decide` refused everywhere under the project namespace except an `Explore` namespace nothing tags or cites. Rational witnesses close by `decide +kernel`. No Mathlib unless a named theorem cannot close without it.

**Assumptions.** Provider behaviour, PostgreSQL semantics and the single engine are named hypotheses on the theorems that use them; a model that omits a second engine says so in its docstring. Never an `axiom`.

**Vocabulary.** Specification gate, witness, model, assumption, property as defined in the glossary. **Reference model** is added to the glossary with M2, the first lifecycle model. *Oracle* stays banned. A settlement parameter is never named *target*.

**Modules.** One module per model, shared identity and outcome types in one place, witnesses in one module, the gate executable unchanged in role. Every module imported by the root, which the wrapper enforces.

## Testing Decisions

- The seam is `check-all.sh`: `lake build`, `lake exe gate`, the Python gates. Nothing else tests the formal layer.
- A good test is a property of external behaviour: a theorem about what the definitions imply for every input, or a decided witness over a concrete trace. Never a test of a proof's internals or a tactic's shape.
- Every guard has its pair: refused with the guard, admitted without. A model with only the positive theorem is incomplete.
- Every model has a successful execution witness (a create that succeeds, a cancellation that destroys) so that a model that refuses everything cannot satisfy its safety theorems vacuously.
- Every new check gets a CI negative control that mutates the thing the check guards, asserts the build or gate went red, and asserts the red came from that check and not from a syntax error or a missing toolchain. `ci.yml` holds the list. Prior art: the four Lean controls and the four textual controls already there.
- Bounded exploration publishes its bounds; it is evidence within them and not an unbounded theorem.
- A theorem never counts toward conformance coverage; the coverage gate reads nothing from the formal layer.

## Out of Scope

- An implementation oracle or a refinement proof; comparing a future implementation to the model is a test, and building that comparison waits for an implementation.
- Aeneas, Verso, or any documentation-platform migration.
- Formalizing provider behaviour, PostgreSQL, deployment, cryptographic hardness, or legal and commercial obligations beyond naming them as hypotheses.
- Rewriting the textual Python gates in Lean.
- Telling tenants a restore interval is running (decided against, `STO-54`).
- Wire fixture generation until M4's evidence is in.

## Further Notes

The panel that shaped this — Codex at xhigh and a fresh Fable reader on one brief — both warned that the fence model built without the claim model, the rate-outage branch, the suspended-tenant branch and the episode proves a false requirement; M3 depends on M2 for that reason and not for convenience. The same panel found by running Lean that `decide` sticks on rational equalities and that `decide +kernel` closes them under the standard axioms; that is why the trust policy can refuse `native_decide` outright.

This set's own record is that each fix round introduces defects at about the rate it removes them and that green gates are not the check. Every milestone therefore ends with a two-axis review of its diff before the next begins.
